note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after f6c2374f02). RFC 5216 Section 5.3: "it SHOULD support validating the peer certificate using RFC 3280 [RFC3280] compliant path validation, including the ability to retrieve intermediate certificates that may be necessary to validate the peer certificate.  For details, see Section 4.2.2.1 of [RFC3280]." The cited section is Authority Information Access, the fetch. The next paragraph names the alternatives for a server that does NOT meet this: "Where the EAP-TLS server is unable to retrieve intermediate certificates, either it will need to be pre-configured with the necessary intermediate certificates to complete path validation or it will rely on the EAP-TLS peer to provide this information". f6c2374f02 implements the first alternative: the intermediate-certificate list (responder_eap.go eapTLSServerConfig) feeds clientChainVerifier.verify (client_chain.go), which path-validates against ca-certificate roots only, with configured plus peer-sent certificates as Intermediates, clientAuth EKU and the current time, and newTLSMethod (eap_tls.go) runs it in VerifyConnection on TLS 1.2, 1.3 and resumed sessions before checkChainRevocation. The tagged tests prove that alternative well (mutants putting the pool in Roots, dropping EKU, time or revocation, or ignoring the verify error each go red). They do not prove retrieval, because the code performs none: no AIA caIssuers lookup exists in internal/core/eap or internal/component/ike, and verify's own comment says Ze retrieves nothing over the network. Pre-configuration is the RFC's named fallback for a server unable to retrieve, not this SHOULD, so the row stays an implementation gap (a SHOULD deviation, not a defect). The row needs its {gap} annotation restored (naming AIA retrieval absent and pre-configuration implemented), and Support remaining must stop saying RFC5216-5.3-5 is no longer among the gaps.
